question.text: Due diligence review (DDR) in an AIF investment typically covers which areas?

answer.text: Legal, financial, tax, technical, and market due diligence
Only the investee company's stock price history

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, the DDR is structured around three components: Business/Commercial/Technical DDR, Financial DDR (which includes tax records, filings, assessments and potential tax demands), and Legal DDR. Together, these components cover the legal, financial, tax, technical and market dimensions of an investee company. The Trap: A DDR limited to a single dimension misses risks that the workbook expressly assigns to other components — for example, tax exposure sits inside Financial DDR rather than Legal DDR. Note: The depth and rigour of the DDR process is one of the elements investors use to differentiate fund managers.
